fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Science Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A science quiz tests what someone knows about the natural world. Emergent builds the questions and the scoring from a prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Questions tagged by strand

Name the unit and grade, such as 8th-grade forces, and Emergent writes each question with one right option and three wrong ones. Each is tagged life, physical, or earth science.
fields.feature_2:
A reason and a source under each answer

Give each question a one-line explanation and a source link. The results screen shows both after the last answer, so a student who disputes a point can check the page.
fields.feature_3:
Every answer saved as a row

Each answer lands in a database you own, stored with the player and the question's science strand. Sort the table by question to find the one a class keeps getting wrong.
fields.feature_4:
One question per phone screen

Players see one question at a time, so a 10-year-old in a museum hall can finish on a phone without zooming in. Emergent puts no cap on how many people take the quiz.
fields.feature_5:
A pass mark that triggers an email

Set a pass mark, such as 10 of 10 on a lab rules quiz, and the app emails the teacher each student below it. Send the alert to a Slack channel when a department needs it.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Run the quiz on a school domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Science Quizzes, Four Different Jobs
fields.tab_content_1:
Students under 10 of 10 retake before the first lab

Before anyone at Harlow Ridge High School lights a burner, all 112 chemistry students take a 10-question lab rules quiz on their phones. The pass mark is 10 of 10. This fall, 14 students fell short, and Tamsin Doyle, who teaches all 4 sections, got an email naming each one. All 14 retook the quiz before Thursday's first lab.
fields.tab_content_2:
The hottest planet question was missed in 702 plays

Kids visiting the planet hall at the Halvorsen Science Center open a 12-question space quiz from a sign by the door and answer one question per screen. October brought 1,240 plays. The question on which planet is hottest was missed in 702 of them, more than any other. Staff then put a card next to the Venus model.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of the 3 strands, physical science gained least

The 38 students at the Sutter Pines Homeschool Co-op take the same 15 questions in September and again in May, 5 per strand. Every answer is saved with its strand. The average rose to 11.2 of 15, up from 6.8. Physical science rose just 1.3 points, the smallest gain of the 3 strands. Next fall opens with a physics unit.
fields.tab_content_4:
96 campers land in 3 groups by score

Elkmont STEM Camp gives campers aged 9 to 12 a 12-question placement quiz. A score of 10 or more goes to Lab Crew, 6 to 9 to Builders, and 5 or under to Explorers. This summer, 23 of the 96 campers went to Lab Crew, 42 to Builders, and 31 to Explorers. The director, Ingrid Paulsen, gets each roster by email.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Science Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a science quiz with fair options, a source for each answer, and results that show which topics to reteach.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the topic and the grade
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Cite a source for each answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name what the quiz covers, such as 6th-grade life science or the solar system, and who will take it. Put both in your prompt, and Emergent drafts questions in words that reader already knows.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each question a strand tag, such as life, physical, or earth and space science. The tags let the results table group answers by topic, which shows a class weak in forces even when its total score looks fine.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the correct option first, then three wrong ones a student could reasonably pick. A question on the largest planet should offer four planets, not one planet and three moons. An option nobody would choose is a free point.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under each question, add one line that explains the answer and a link to where it comes from, such as a NASA fact page or a textbook chapter. Show both on the results screen, where a student who disagrees can check them.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set bands that cover every score
fields.howto_step_5_des: For a 10-question quiz, pick 3 bands such as 0 to 4, 5 to 7, and 8 to 10, and write a short message for each that names what to review. Check that every possible score falls into exactly one band before launch.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have 3 students take the quiz on their phones before the whole class does. If all 3 miss a question the same way, reread its wording before you blame the science, and check that their answers reached the table.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the unit, give the same quiz again and compare each strand's average with the first round. The strand that moved least is where the next lesson starts, and the table keeps both rounds side by side.

faq_plan.a: A science quiz is a set of questions that tests what someone knows about living things and the physical world. Each question has one correct answer, and the score shows which topics a player knows well and which to study again.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a science quiz?
faq_plan.a: Choose the topic and the grade, write each question with one correct option and three believable wrong ones, tag it by strand, and set score bands. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe that quiz in a prompt and get a working app that scores each player and saves every answer to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How many science quiz questions should one class quiz have?
faq_plan.a: For a quiz that fits in one class period, 10 to 15 questions is a workable length. Decide the count per strand before you write, such as 5 each for life, physical, and earth science in a 15-question quiz. That keeps any one topic from deciding the score.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find science quiz questions and answers I can trust?
faq_plan.a: Write them yourself from primary sources, such as NASA's planet fact pages, MedlinePlus for the human body, and the textbook your class uses. Put the source link under each answer, as the quiz on this page does, and anyone who doubts an answer can check it.

faq_plan.q: What makes a science quiz for kids different from one for adults?
faq_plan.a: It needs shorter questions and plainer words. For a science quiz for kids aged 8 to 12, keep each question under 15 words, offer 3 or 4 options, and show the explanation right after each answer. Emergent builds conversational quizzes with one question per screen, which suits a small phone.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free science quiz for my class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. You can describe the quiz, share its link with your class, and read every answer in the results table without paying first.

faq_plan.q: Should a science quiz use multiple choice or true or false questions?
faq_plan.hint: A science quiz has eight multiple choice questions?
faq_plan.a: Use multiple choice for most of it. A true or false question gives a guesser a 1 in 2 chance of a point, while four options cut that to 1 in 4. Keep true or false for quick checks of a single fact.

faq_plan.q: How do I grade a science quiz by topic instead of by total score?
faq_plan.a: Tag each question with its topic when you write it, then group the results by that tag. A class can score 12 of 15 overall and still miss most of the forces questions. A quiz app built with Emergent keeps answers in your own database, where grouping them by tag takes one sort.

faq_plan.q: How often should I give a science quiz during a unit?
faq_plan.a: Give one short quiz at the start of a unit to find gaps and the same quiz at the end to measure growth. A 5-question check in the middle catches a misunderstanding while there is still time to reteach it.

faq_plan.q: How do I write a science quiz question that tests understanding, not memory?
faq_plan.a: Describe a situation and ask which idea explains it, instead of asking for a definition. Rather than asking students to name a force, show a sled slowing on flat snow and ask what slows it. A student who memorized a word list cannot answer that by recall alone.

quiz.title: Science Quiz: 8 Questions on Planets, Cells, and Gravity
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the planets, Earth's air and tides, gravity, cells, and the human body. Pick one answer for each; your score and a source for every answer show at the end.

questions.text: Which planet is the hottest in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Its thick atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, and surface temperatures reach about 872 degrees Fahrenheit.

source.quote: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system

questions.text: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is so large that, if it were a hollow shell, 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.

source.quote: Jupiter is a world of extremes. It's the largest planet in our solar system

questions.text: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up 78% of the air, oxygen 21%, and other gases such as argon the last 1%.

source.quote: Earth's atmosphere is 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and 1% other ingredients

questions.text: What force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the force by which a planet or other body pulls objects toward its center, and the Sun's gravity holds the planets in their orbits.

source.quote: The force of gravity keeps all of the planets in orbit around the sun

questions.text: What causes the ocean tides on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravitational pull draws the seas toward it, and that pull is what raises the tides.

source.quote: The gravitational pull of the moon pulls the seas towards it, causing the ocean tides

questions.text: Which part of a cell generates most of its chemical energy?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria store the energy they produce in a small molecule called ATP, which powers the cell's reactions.

source.quote: Mitochondria are membrane-bound cell organelles (mitochondrion, singular) that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions

questions.text: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Your skin covers the entire outside of your body and protects it in several ways.

source.quote: Your skin is your body's largest organ

questions.text: What is the only planet known to be inhabited by living things?
questions.explanation: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only place known so far to support life.

source.quote: It's the only place we know of inhabited by living things
